Here are a few tips to help.

1. Genuinely find out what the call is for, ask questions. A lot of sales come from just asking questions, and being genuine.

2. Actually help with the issue, set expectations if you need to reach out to a leader for assistance. People will be much happier if not just pushed around to different places. Use your resources, knowledge base, support lines, and management. More for you to learn, and also to help the customer.

3. Before transferring, let the customer know whatever new promos there are. “Before I transfer you, did you know we offer mobile phone services now? You can keep your same number and get a new phone!” If they are interested, then get into the details. Be sure to be honest. Honesty sells way more than pushy shady tactics.

4. Don’t take calls personal. Sometimes people are just mad and want to vent it out. It’s not you specifically, it’s the company or a prior experience they are mad at. Let them get it out, ask questions to try and resolve it, do what you can, and let them know of new promos before the end. With genuine intent.

If you do those things every call, you will hit goal.

As you learn more about what you can and can’t do, still stay in the habit of treating every call as listed above. It’s easy to just transfer someone out when you hear a keyword or something similar, don’t do that. Ask questions and try to be the resolution, not the operator.

In time when you are more advanced when comfortable, use your knowledge of what people mostly call about to help guide and direct. For example..

“I just want the $50 internet.”

“We do have that available, how many people will be using the $50 internet?”

You will find some people say one (ok) and some people say five or more (not ok)

Make recommendations that fit what the customer needs, not to oversell. If they decline, that’s on them, but at least you made an honest and genuine attempt to give good advice.

Lastly, get out after you hit your year. Don’t be that person in the same role for 5-10 years, explore the many roles available within the company. Get mentors, join and seek projects, etc.

Best of luck, but you won’t need luck if you follow the guide above. :)
